title: Canonical pullback map of relative differential sheaves
statement: Let $h:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to S$ be morphisms of schemes. Write $\Omega_{Y/S}$ and $\Omega_{X/S}$ for the relative differential sheaves [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf], with their universal derivations $d$, and use tensor module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. There exists a unique morphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules $d_{h/S}:h^*\Omega_{Y/S}\to\Omega_{X/S}$ such that, for every open $W\subseteq Y$ and $a\in\mathcal O_Y(W)$, it sends the pulled-back section $1\otimes da$ over $h^{-1}(W)$ to $d(h^\sharp(a))$. Here $1\otimes da$ is the image in the sheafified tensor product of the pure tensor of $1$ with the image of $da$ under the unit of the abelian inverse-image adjunction. The canonical differential map $d_{h/S}$ is this unique morphism.

source.place: Tag 01UV, lemma-functoriality-differentials, specialization to identity on the base S; unique characterization on local functions

proof.text: Compose the universal derivation of Omega_(X/S) with h-sharp on each open of Y. The Leibniz rule follows from multiplicativity of h-sharp; restriction compatibility follows from its naturality and that of the universal derivation. It vanishes on functions from S because h-sharp composed with g-sharp is (h composed with g)-sharp. Scheme.Hom.derivationMk therefore gives an S-relative derivation into h_* Omega_(X/S). Apply Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentialsHomEquiv from [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf] to obtain q : Omega_(Y/S) -> h_* Omega_(X/S), with q(da) = d(h-sharp(a)).

Use the section-normalized adjunction exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction of [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction]. Its hom equivalence e sends d to the map evaluating d on the sheafified tensor 1 tensor the abelian inverse-image unit, precisely the generator in this node. The inverse image e.symm(q) has the required generator formula by the inverse laws and relativeDifferentialsHomEquiv_symm_app_d. If another d has that formula, e(d) and q induce identical derivations on every function. Injectivity of relativeDifferentialsHomEquiv gives e(d)=q, and injectivity of e proves uniqueness.

proof_origin.place: Tag 01UV, lemma-functoriality-differentials; the adjunction and its section formula are Tag 0096, lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules, in sheaves.tex
